html:
The Squamish, who call themselves Skwxwú7mesh, are a Coast Salish people of Howe Sound and the Squamish River valley, north of today's Vancouver in British Columbia. Skwxwú7mesh-ulh Temíx̱w means "Squamish land".

They lived in villages along the sound and the river, fishing salmon, hunting and gathering, and travelling by canoe. Their neighbours were the Musqueam and Tsleil-Waututh around Burrard Inlet and the St'át'imc inland. Smallpox struck them hard in the late 1700s and again in 1862. As Vancouver grew, they lost village sites such as Kitsilano. In 1906 their chief Joe Capilano travelled to London to press the king about their land. The Squamish Nation was formed in 1923 by joining many villages.
